newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks Mobutu-Kabila meeting on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France seeks Mobutu-Kabila meeting on Zaire.

text.p: France called for the first time on Friday for embattled Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko to meet rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces have captured about a third of the country, to negotiate a peaceful transition to democracy.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a daily briefing: "Such a meeting could facilitate a peaceful solution, which is what we all want."

Mobutu has so far refused Kabila's demands for face-to-face talks. The rebels, who have captured most of the country's mineral resources and its second biggest city, Lubumbashi, have said they are only prepared to negotiate Mobutu's departure.
France, which has long backed Mobutu, has sought to distance itself from the ageing, cancer-stricken strongman in the last few days.
Asked if Paris was in contact with Kabila, Rummelhardt said France had "contacts with all the parties in Zaire".
He continued to call for a ceasefire despite statements saying a military outcome would in no way consolidate civil peace or national reconciliation in Zaire.
